relevance_note: Case report of a man with a homozygous LCAT variant: "A case of homozygous familial lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) deficiency with a novel homozygous LCAT missense mutation"; the Discussion also gives individual-level facts on earlier-published LCAT-deficient patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans verbatim. No tables in the paper. Scope: the proband ('patient'; 'index case'/'proband' are role words), six relatives described in relation to him (parents described as obligate heterozygotes; four siblings with HDL values), and previously published LCAT-deficient people given individual-level facts in the Discussion: the 1967 Norum and Gjone patient (^13–15) and her two similarly affected sisters, the Maeda et al^9 patient, the 'second case' with codon 293 mutations (labelled 'unnamed person 1' because the sentence cites both Maeda et al^9 and Gotoda et al.^10 and does not make clear which reference describes this person; source_reference left 'not reported'), and the two Japanese patients of refs 28 and 29. The four Jimi et al^21 patients are described only as a group and get no rows. Relatives were not genotyped (parents 'obligate heterozygotes', a brother and sister 'probable heterozygotes' from HDL levels), so they have no variant rows. The 43-year-old sister's HDL of 37 mg/dL and the 51-year-old brother's HDL of 62 mg/dL are not labelled low or normal for a named person, so low HDL is not reported for them; the paper's 'two siblings are normal' does not name which two. Proband: no protein or cDNA HGVS strings are printed; the variant is described in prose (T-to-G change in exon 6; ATG to AGG at codon 293; methionine to arginine at 293). Inheritance left 'not reported' because the parents were not tested (described as obligate heterozygotes). APOE3/3 genotype and Factor V Leiden -/- results were not recorded as variants (common/negative findings). Possible contradiction: the proband 'had no history of coronary disease' yet 'does, therefore, have some evidence of mild coronary artery disease' (coronary calcium score 90) and 'no evidence of clinically significant CHD'; both feature rows were emitted and the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease checklist item was set to 'not reported'. Elevated unesterified cholesterol was left 'not reported' for the proband and the Norum patient: the paper gives the unesterified share (19% esterified; 'most of the cholesterol ... unesterified'), recorded as reduced cholesteryl ester fraction, not an absolute free-cholesterol elevation. Normal findings were recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27), e.g. 'normal kidney function' for the Norum patient excludes renal failure. The ref 29 patient was on dialysis for 7 years, but the text does not state renal failure, so that checklist item is 'not reported'. 'unnamed person 1' was 'heterozygous for two separate mutations': recorded as compound heterozygous; one variant row for the Met293Ile variant identical to Maeda's patient (spans from two sentences), one row 'not reported' for the second, undescribed mutation. The sister of the proband aged 43 is printed '43 yeas of age' (typo kept verbatim). Discussion note: 'this diagnosis is ruled in the index' about apoA-I deficiency appears to be a typo for 'ruled out'; not used.
